summary: Configured node1 so only root and opsadmin can use cron. The policy persisted across a verified node restart; AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the local opsadmin account with a locked password.
Installed /etc/cron.allow containing exactly root and opsadmin, owned by root:root with mode 0600.
Verified root and opsadmin can access crontab while nobody is rejected.
Safely restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed.
Confirmed crond, the account, access policy, and enforcement recovered after restart.

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin may schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: The allow-list contains exactly root and opsadmin. Direct crontab tests permit both listed users and reject nobody before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 were unchanged; no platform software was upgraded.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart and recovery for node1
evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline boot ID 4a743885-c59f-43ee-afde-ef96f7bea723, acknowledged a native scheduled reboot, observed new boot ID 779c0f5b-88b3-4e8b-a2f4-18150641069b, and verified the system, crond, policy data, user, and enforcement recovered.
